Both halves hold on 96084 (raw TL: one PageBlockParagraph carrying TextUrl `tg://document?id=doc0`, one bubble, no twin). The earlier FAIL scored the probe on `documents: []` and was WRONG: ADR §4.2 records the client measurement (2026-11-12) that the LINK form is the form that is visible and opens, while the EMBED form drew nothing. L9.note: CLAIM CORRECTED 2026-11-14, verdict left FAIL. The original claim demanded THREE distinct media ENTRIES, but ADR §4.2 measures that a document deliberately rides as a LINK-FORM REFERENCE and never as an entry (the embed form draws nothing in the client). So the honest claim is: one bubble, image bound as a photo entry, video bound as a video entry, document present as a link reference. Measured on 96248 (raw TL): ONE bubble ✓, photo entry ✓ (5456183027160524023), video ✗ (left as TextUrl `tg://video?id=vid0`, `documents: []`), document link ✓ by design. The video half is the real defect: the shield demoted the rewriter's own `![...](tg://video?id=vid0)` embed because it judged image syntax photo-only. Fixed in 2b9789721; this verdict stays FAIL until a post-ship re-probe measures the fixed binary.

L11.note: §2 rule 2 is not met on this message. The emit is EMBED for video (r6-photo-and-video-emit-embed passes statically), so this is not the link-form artefact L8 records — an embed-syntax video entry still failed to bind beside a photo that did. Two readings remain open and this probe does not separate them: (a) a video entry is dropped when it shares a message with a photo, or (b) the 64-byte fixture was refused. §4.1 measured a 46 848-byte mp4 delivering PageBlockVideo, so (b) is live and must be excluded by re-probing with a full-size mp4 before any code change is attributed. RE-PROBE OWED: the root cause was found after this measurement - pipeline pass 2 (`shield_unresolvable_markdown_images`) judged image syntax photo-only and stripped the `!` from the rewriter's own `![...](tg://video?id=vid0)`, and a link binds nothing for any kind. Fixed in 2b9789721 (kind-aware: Photo->photo scheme, Video->tg://video scheme, Document->never). This FAIL is the PRE-FIX repro; a post-ship re-probe of the same reply re-scores it.

L16.note: §2 rule 1's size split is honoured on the tool plane and MISSING from the rich rewriter. src/utils/image.rs claimed every locally-valid image as 'tg://photo' with no size check, so a 12 MiB PNG went out as a photo, Telegram refused it with the 400 above, the entry was sacrificed and the whole message fell back to the html dialect -- the reader got a dead '!' plus a link instead of a document bubble. Fixed in 8446abd66: the image family now declines a reference above TELEGRAM_PHOTO_MAX_BYTES (10 MiB) and hands it to the file family, which emits link-form '[alt](tg://document?id=docN)'; bytes_owned_by_an_earlier_family carries the same wall so the file family is not blocked from taking the hand-off. Both planes now read ONE constant. This verdict is the PRE-FIX repro and owes a post-ship re-probe.

L17.method: direct Bot API sendRichMessage, multipart, one form per message
L17.probe: A/B: identical media entry {type:document, media:attach://docN} with real bytes; the ONLY variable is the markdown reference form.

form_embed.result: BOUND - the document entry is attached and rendered as a document block

form_link.result: DROPPED - the entry is discarded and the reference degrades to a bare link

L17.note: Both legs returned HTTP 200 and both carried a real multipart part (attach://docN). The link leg's entry is silently discarded by the server: no error, no warning. This is the measured reason the owner reports 'the link is not clickable' - the link form has nothing behind it. ADR 4.2's claim that the link form is the one that renders is FALSIFIED by this measurement; 4.1's table (embed delivered, link delivered nothing) is confirmed.
L17.conclusion: Document references MUST be emitted in EMBED form with a bound media entry. The link form is a dead reference. #827's flip to link form was the wrong direction; the shield that demotes a matching document embed to link form is a defect.
